newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IMF loan could aid S.Africa credibility - Old Mutual.
newsitem.headline: IMF loan could aid S.Africa credibility - Old Mutual.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) loan could help South Africa's credibility offshore but existing pressure points in the economy would remain, leading life assurance group Old Mutual said on Thursday.
"Yes, IMF assistance would improve the credibility of the South African government in the eyes of investors but (existing) pressures in the economy will remain," chief economist Dave Mohr said.

Speaking at an economic presentation, Mohr said IMF fund facilities would likely see some stability return to the currency market but he questioned the extent to which it would change the fundamental economic picture.
"Also, the cash injection could disappear quickly in the market," he said.
Factors exerting pressure on the rand were remaining exchange controls, negative sentiment locally and offshore, and the current account situation, he said.

"For government to improve its credibility it needs to surprise in terms of the implementation of its Growth, Employment and Redistribution strategy...we need further action to ensure the current account closes and an aggressive announcement on privatisation," Mohr said.
He said in reality the rand was starting to take account of the abolition of exchange controls on residents.
However, unless there was convincing action from the government on privatisation, the budget deficit and the current account, the rand was unlikely to stabilise.
Calls mounted this week for South Africa to seek IMF assistance as the rand continued to sink to new all-time lows against the dollar.
However, in Thursday trade it managed to bounce back seven cents below the 4.70 level as speculators took profits.

Under IMF rules, South Africa would be able to draw up to 100 percent of its IMF quota -- or some $2 billion -- for use as a standby or extended fund facility. -- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom +2711 482 1003
